title: Aave rsETH precautionary freeze after a Kelp fee-minter over-mint (30 Apr 2025), near-miss control
summary: At 06:16:59 UTC on 30 Apr 2025 a faulty Kelp LRTOracle upgrade minted about 1.7×10^16 rsETH to Kelp's fee address, multiplying rsETH totalSupply by about 3×10^10. rsETH's own circuit breaker blocked the exchange-rate update and paused deposits and withdrawals; Kelp paused contracts at 07:51, posted at 08:55, and burned the excess at 15:40. Aave's Guardian froze rsETH on Core at 10:03 (LTV 72% → 0) and BGD posted at 10:36 that Aave was not affected. Aave's rsETH oracle never moved (1.04329 ETH), WETH utilization stayed 86–88%, and the rsETH market price stayed about 1.04 ETH. rsETH was unfrozen on 8 May. Nobody on Aave lost money or got stuck: a near-miss that looked alarming on-chain.

positions_considered.description: Supplies WETH on Aave V3 Core, no debt
WETH collateral with USDC debt on Aave V3 Core, health factor about 1.6
rsETH collateral with WETH debt in the rsETH e-mode on Aave V3 Core (leveraged loop, health factor about 1.02–1.05)

t_first_public_signal.description: The mint itself is visible on-chain (rsETH totalSupply ×3e10). First text: Kelp X post 08:55:22. First Aave action: rsETH freeze 10:03:47. A monitor watching only Aave reserves sees nothing until 10:03:47.

t_point_of_no_return.definition: None reached. WETH utilization never exceeded 88.9% (no withdrawal constraint), Aave's rsETH oracle never moved, and no liquidations or bad debt followed. A PONR would have been an exchange-rate drop past the e-mode liquidation threshold, or WETH utilization ≥ 99%.

t_protocol_first_ack.description: Aave Guardian freezes rsETH on Core (on-chain); BGD forum post 10:36:57. Kelp: on-chain pause 07:51:59, X post 08:55:22.

other_markers.name: morpho_curator_delist
other_markers.description: Steakhouse removes rsETH exposure on Morpho (peer risk manager exits).

lead_time_minutes.notes: No PONR. Mint → Kelp pause 95 min; mint → Kelp post 158 min; mint → Aave freeze 227 min; mint → BGD 'not affected' 260 min; mint → burn 564 min.

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: No effect. WETH utilization 86.1–88.9% for 29 Apr – 9 May; full withdrawals possible throughout.
No effect. Health factor unchanged; USDC utilization 69–79%.

No liquidation; the oracle stayed 1.04329 ETH. Could not add rsETH collateral while frozen (8 days) and could not redeem through Kelp while it was paused, but could repay WETH, withdraw rsETH and sell it near fair value (~1.04 ETH) at any time.
outcome_passive_holder.stuck_duration: none for exit; new collateral blocked 30 Apr 10:03 – 8 May 14:44

ground_truth.outcome_price_only_rule: No trigger. ETH/USD and rsETH/ETH were stable (rsETH/ETH 1.037–1.050 on DeFiLlama; Aave oracle constant), and no health factor moved. A price-only rule behaves correctly here: no false alarm.

ideal_action.rationale: No transmission path to WETH liquidity or solvency appeared; utilization flat.
No exposure beyond the shared pool; no stress.

In hindsight hold was optimal. A light reduction in the first hours (before BGD's 10:36 statement) would have cost only swap fees and some carry, so reduce_light is an acceptable judge answer until 10:36.

expected_judge_labels.rationale: A collateral-token anomaly with no sign of transmission: oracle unchanged, WETH utilization flat, no new rsETH borrows. 'elevated/hold' is a tolerable answer here; any reduce/exit is a false alarm.
Aave confirmed unaffected; exposure capped by freeze.
No stress on WETH or USDC; health factor unchanged.

The collateral token's supply exploded and Kelp paused redemptions; a high-leverage loop has little buffer if the exchange rate were hit. Reducing was cheap (rsETH at fair value, WETH liquid). 'elevated/hold' is equally acceptable.
Aave says unaffected; excess burned 15:40; asset frozen but price and oracle stable.

items.notes: Created 11:17:46Z, edited 11:23:00Z (version 2). Its times mix time zones: '06:16am UTC' matches the on-chain mint, but '10:55am UTC' for Kelp's update matches the tweet snowflake (08:55:22Z) only as UTC+2, and the '12:30/12:31/12:37pm UTC' actions come after the post's own creation time unless they are also UTC+2 (10:30–10:37Z). Treat the cited times as CEST mislabelled as UTC. Venue differs (Morpho), but an Aave-position monitor reading curator forums would see it. This is a 'delist' action by a peer risk manager: the strongest alarm in the window.

items.author: woz (Morpho forum)
items.verbatim_text: We’d like to add a comment on the Kelp Incident that Steakhouse posted about last week . Due to a bug in the fee minter, an excess amount of tokens was unintentionally minted and ended up in Kelp’s fee recipient address. We’re fortunate this didn’t impact the rsETH exchange rate; if it had, and without the proposed system architecture, the curators’ vaults could have faced significantly higher risk.

items.author: BGD Labs
items.verbatim_text: As a follow-up to the community, we would like to elaborate on the incident last week and what we think is the appropriate next step. As aforementioned, on April 30th, Kelp DAO had a bug on rsETH after an upgrade of one of its smart contracts. The contract involved was the so-called LRTOracle , which, amongst others, is in charge of recalculating/exposing the exchange rate of rsETH to its underlying, and other secondary mechanisms like fee accrual to the Kelp DAO treasury. data_gaps: No mainstream news coverage with a publish time found. Google News RSS for 28 Apr – 10 May 2025 returned nothing relevant. bitcoinworld.co.in/kelp-dao-pauses-rs-eth/ (dated 30 Apr 2025 per search snippet) now returns HTTP 410.
Kelp's 30 Apr 2025 note tweet is truncated at 280 characters in the syndication copy.
No security-firm X posts (PeckShield, Cyvers and others) about this event were found.
The names of Kelp contracts 0x036676… and 0x62de59… were not read on-chain (roles inferred).
Not in the DeFiLlama hacks feed (no loss).
rsETH e-mode parameters on Core in April 2025 were not decoded; looper HF range is an assumption.
source_quality: High for the timeline. All on-chain times, supplies, oracle ratios and reserve states come from our own archive RPC reads. Forum times come from Discourse JSON; the Kelp X time comes from the snowflake. The Steakhouse Morpho post has internally inconsistent time zones (documented). Thin news coverage is itself informative: the event barely registered outside forums.
